title: SOP Sampling General Recommendations
author: Melanie Van Weddingen
materials: Separate the sample and the vouchers.

Photography Equipement Ideally, please use high quality material used for scientific photography, with a flash, installed on a stand and with dedicated lightning. If this equipment is not available where you are, you can also use a smartphone attached to a support for stability, and good ad hoc lightning. Always use a scale, such as a ruler graduated in mm and cm, and ensure that it is visible on the photo (no reflection, blurry, etc.) across the length of the specimen. If using professional cameras, here are some general guidelines: Shutter Speed (1/100) : Use fast speeds for live specimens to freeze motion, especially when using flashes. Aperture (F14) : Higher values decrease light entry but increase depth of field, resulting in sharper images. ISO (125) : Adjusts brightness. Higher values increase brightness but add noise, reducing image sharpness. Avoid lenses that cause distortion, such as wide-angle lenses. Use 50 mm or 100 mm macro lenses for specimens larger than 1 cm. Use a 65 mm macro lens for specimens smaller than 1 cm.

steps.title: Define collection station
steps.instruction: Create a unique collection station for each sampling event, recording time t, location (XYZ), field collectors, a single collection method, and a unique station code; do not assign multiple methods to the same station – create separate stations if needed.

steps.title: Enter mandatory metadata
steps.instruction: Complete all metadata columns for the station: Mission name, Station code, Collection method, Locality, Coordinates (decimal degrees to 10⁻⁶, single point or start‑end for transects), Depth (min‑max or start‑end, e.g., “0‑15” m), Datetime (dd/mm/yyyy and hh:mm start/end), Names of collectors with institutions (alphabetical SURNAME Firstname), Habitats, and station photos. Use “NOT_COLLECTED” for any unknown field. For trawling methods fill both “start” and “end” columns. Follow MNHN or temporary coding rules as described.

steps.title: Confirm taxonomic identification
steps.instruction: Have a qualified taxonomist verify the specimen’s morphology, record the taxonomist’s name, then check the accepted species name in WoRMS. Search the species in the GoaT portal, enable “sequencing status” column, and note the assembly level (Reference/Chromosome, Scaffold, Contig) and sequencing status (sample collected, in progress, etc.). Proceed to DNA extraction only if the genome is not already at EBP‑standard level unless approved by the ATLASea Species Selection Committee.

steps.title: Photograph specimens
steps.instruction: Take a reference photo (specimen with ATLASea and MNHN labels plus a ruler) and at least one specimen‑only photo; add anatomical‑detail close‑ups if needed. Use a glass container on a black background (or white for dark animals) or place the animal directly on a solid background. Change seawater between specimens, keep water clean, and return the animal to seawater periodically to reduce stress. Save all images as high‑resolution JPEGs, name them with the MNHN identifier followed by an incremental suffix (e.g., MNHN‑IM‑2019‑515655_01, _02, …), and sort by relevance before sending.

steps.title: Decontaminate instruments
steps.instruction: After each organism, wipe forceps/scalpels with wet absorbent paper, immerse in sterile water for 1 min, then in a 2.6 % active chlorine bleach solution diluted ¼ for 5 min, rinse in sterile water for 5 min, and finish with a quick ethanol dip to dry. Clean work surfaces (e.g., Aniospray + water) and change gloves between organisms.

steps.title: Prepare tissue aliquots
steps.instruction: Work on a cold board (glass on ice tray). Remove visible contaminants, then dissect rapidly. For each taxon prepare at least 15 aliquots: ≥10 pieces for DNA (≈300 mg each for animals, ideally 1 g for algae/plants) and 2–3 RNA tubes containing ~50 mg of mixed recommended tissues. Cut pieces into smaller fragments before placing in separate, uniquely labelled conical‑bottom tubes. Use one specimen per tube for small individuals; avoid compacting the sample or filling the tube to the top. Never pool different individuals in the same tube.

steps.title: Label and weigh tubes
steps.instruction: Apply ATLASea‑provided labels lengthwise on dry tubes (labels must be ethanol‑resistant if later stored in ethanol). Ensure tubes and gloves are dry before labeling. Screw caps tightly, then weigh each tube with cap; use a tare tube of the same model to calculate sample weight. For very small specimens estimate weight using the provided scale. Scan each barcode with the ATLASea log‑sheet app before flash‑freezing and record the data (ask ambassadors@atlasea.fr for the latest sheet).

steps.title: Flash‑freeze and store samples
steps.instruction: Immediately flash‑freeze all aliquoted tubes in liquid nitrogen (LN₂) to prevent nuclease activity, then store at –80 °C. For voucher material, preserve in 80 % ethanol and store at –20 °C. Group ~10 tubes in a nylon bag labelled with a unique number (place same‑taxon tubes together when possible), seal with twist‑ties, and immerse the bag in LN₂ (Dewar). Avoid any freeze‑thaw cycles. Transfer sealed bags to a –80 °C freezer for long‑term storage; if a –80 °C freezer is unavailable in the field, keep bags in a large LN₂ container designed for storage and later move them to ultra‑freezer conditions.

steps.title: Prepare taxonomic vouchers
steps.instruction: After dissection, fix all remaining body parts (e.g., in 85 % ethanol) to serve as vouchers. Label each voucher with ethanol‑resistant MNHN labels; if the specimen is too small and no material remains, fix another individual of the same batch as a “ghost voucher” and keep its labels in a bag marked “ATLASea specimen labels GHOST VOUCHER”. Never discard any label. Include all permits with the vouchers; vouchers cannot be entered into the MNHN collection without them.

steps.title: Arrange shipment of samples
steps.instruction: Contact Genoscope SeqLab staff (Janaina Rigonato jrigonat@genoscope.cns.fr, Karine Labadie klabadie@genoscope.cns.fr, Pedro Oliveira pcoutool@genoscope.cns.fr) and MNHN manager (Mélanie Van Weddingen melanie.van-weddingen@mnhn.fr) to confirm shipping details and send the ATLASea log sheet by email. Pack frozen samples in dry‑shippers or boxes with dry ice (place –80 °C tubes in the middle of the dry ice, ethanol‑preserved –20 °C tubes on top). Separate the sample package from the voucher package. Ship on Mondays or Tuesdays between 08:30 and 16:00; otherwise arrange an alternative with Janaina Rigonato. Send the sample package to 31 Boulevard des Coquibus 91000 Évry, France, and the voucher package to 55 rue Buffon 75005 Paris, France. Include a letter stating the ATLASea project name, sender name, brief sample description, any CITES permits, and a printed copy of the pre‑shipment email (log sheet attached).

steps.title: Send photographs to ATLASea
steps.instruction: Email all JPEG photos (reference, specimen, and anatomical details) to ambassadors@atlasea.fr in one or several batches, or upload them to a shared server and send the download link to the same address. Ensure file names follow the MNHN identifier with incremental suffixes.
